conventions.convention: Over C, D(G) has basis d(h,g), multiplication d(h,g)d(k,l)=1[h=gkg⁻¹]d(h,gl), coproduct Δd(h,g)=Σ(ab=h)d(a,g)⊗d(b,g), antipode S(d(h,g))=d(g⁻¹h⁻¹g,g⁻¹), and adjoint d(h,g)*=d(g⁻¹hg,g⁻¹).

Group elements form an orthonormal edge basis. Gauge transformations send g_a to k_source g_a k_target⁻¹, including conjugation on loops. Face holonomy multiplies edge labels in boundary-walk order, using inverses for reversed traversals.
Cellulations are finite and lie on closed connected surfaces; edge orientations are chosen, but a surface orientation is not assumed.

A sector means an equivalence class of nonzero finite-dimensional irreducible unital complex D(G)-modules. Changing the conjugacy-class representative transports the centralizer representation by conjugation.

The Z₂ example assumes AC for its lattice supplier, restricts crossing strings to the square L×L torus with L≥3, and identifies only finite algebraic signs; it asserts no general braiding or empirical realization.

load_bearing.statement: Defines D(G)=C^G⊗C[G], its basis multiplication, coproduct, counit, unit, antipode, and conjugate-linear adjoint for a finite group G.
For every finite group H, Irr_C(H) is finite and the sum of (dim_C π)² over its irreducible representation classes equals |H|.

The displayed structure maps make D(G) a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over C; the conjugate-linear adjoint is an involution reversing multiplication, preserves coproduct and unit, and satisfies ε(a*)=overline(ε(a)).

Irreducible finite-dimensional D(G)-modules are classified by pairs (C,[π]) consisting of a conjugacy class and an irreducible complex representation of its representative's centralizer. Their dimensions are |C|dim π, and their squared dimensions sum to |G|².
Defines vertex gauge permutations, their normalized averages A_v, diagonal face-flatness projections B_f, and H_Σ=Σ_v(I−A_v)+Σ_f(I−B_f) on the finite configuration Hilbert space.

concerns.concern: The diagram Remarks call a₁a₂a₃⁻¹a₄⁻¹ the “clockwise boundary walk from v₀.” With the displayed coordinates, this walk goes right, up, left, down and is counterclockwise. The edge directions, holonomy formula, and conjugation calculation agree with one another; only the orientation word is wrong.

seams_checked.note: Read the supplier page and its four items. The A-page requires it as background but makes no additional textual claim about its results. The finite-group lattice construction is defined independently and does not import the toric supplier's orientability, genus, or spectral-gap conclusions.

The example uses the supplier's square-torus coordinate cycles with intersection one and its exact crossing sign (−1)^I. It retains L≥3 and the supplier's AC assumption, and limits the comparison to equality of algebraic signs. The source and consuming statements agree.
